observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The instructor provides calm, step-by-step guidance, focusing heavily on upper body posture and distinct arm versus leg rhythms. She breaks down movements verbally while demonstrating slowly before applying them to music.

lesson_structure.note: Teacher introduces the Lezginka female workshop
Explains hand positioning and finger posture
Discusses upper body isolation and posture
Combines arm and leg movements slowly without traveling
Practices the steps along with music

metaphors: Imagine that you are touching something
common_mistakes: Dropping or not fixing the fingers
Moving shoulders, neck, and head instead of isolating the upper body
Moving arms too fast or bouncing around

steps_taught.name: Basic Lezginka Footwork
steps_taught.description: Small quick steps in place with legs close together

steps_taught.name: Arm Port de Bras
steps_taught.description: Soft fluid arm and elbow movement leading the hands

what_works: Isolating upper body and leg instruction before combining them
Showing what not to do contrasted with correct posture
what_hinders: Detailed verbal explanations can sometimes become repetitive

quotes.text: Now we're going to try to learn Lezginka dance.
The basic thing is that we should keep our fingers like this.
The thing is that legs make their movement in their own rhythm and hands are very soft.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher stands facing the camera in a studio setting, introducing the workshop verbally.
Teacher holds her hands up and adjusts finger positions to demonstrate correct hand shape.
Teacher turns to the side to show arm and elbow movement initiation.
Teacher demonstrates leg tapping exercise while keeping the upper body still.

extraction.distinctive_method: Emphasizing the isolation and contrasting speeds between fast leg movements and soft, slow hand movements.
